notes:
Summary: Lantern Grove is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a latency-sensitive chat + reranking workload supporting their retail-banking product. They need predictable p95 token latency and committed throughput for business SLAs (customer-facing chat and fraud detection signals).

Key requirements / ask: 
- Target: p95 per-token latency <= 80ms for chat at steady state; ephemeral spikes allowed up to 180ms but must be covered by SLA fallback policy.
- Throughput: baseline 450 requests/minute (approx 7.5 rps) for 1K concurrent chat sessions during peak; burst capacity to 1,800 r/min for marketing pushes.
- Reserved planning: want recommendation for reserved GPU mix. Preference for H100 for top-tier production paths, but cost-sensitivity asks for mixed pool (H100 + A100 spot/dedicated) with clear routing rules.
- Autoscaling & capacity mgmt: require explicit scale-up/down policy review — cannot scale-to-zero for main pool, want warm pool of idle instances to remove cold-starts; target warm pool capacity for 10% of peak (approx 2 nodes in current POC).
- Queueing behavior: need backpressure guarantees; Redwood to outline queued request limits, FIFO vs priority queue options, and fallback to lower-cost model variant when queue length > threshold.
- Batching & latency tradeoffs: use workload-aware batching with tight latency caps; prefer continuous KV cache to reduce token generation cost for repeated contexts.
- SLA negotiations: Lantern Grove expects SLA credit language for latency SLO misses and a documented escalation path (SE + CSM + support on-call). They prefer monthly uptime and p95 latency guarantees by route/model.

POC findings so far: 
- 2-week POC (4xH100) shows median token latency ~35ms, p95 ~95ms under synthetic chat load with 128-token responses; when batching aggressively p95 improved but tail suffers during arrival bursts.
- Observed queueing spike when burst > warm pool + autoscale ramp — requests experienced queued delay ~600ms while new instances spun up.
- Warm pool (kept at 2 nodes) reduced cold-starts by ~70% in POC; still need documented warm-pool sizing guidelines for multi-region setup.

Direct quotes: "If we can't get firm throughput guarantees for peak marketing pushes, procurement won't sign the 2-year commit," — Director of Ops.
"We care more about tail latency than median — a frustrated customer is a lost deposit," — Head of Product.

Open questions for Redwood team: 
- Recommend reserved GPU mix and sizing per region (NA + EU) with cost delta scenarios.
- Provide explicit autoscale policy examples (scale thresholds, cool-downs, max parallel launches) and expected ramp durations per GPU type.
- Define queueing thresholds and suggested fallback model-routing rules with cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Draft SLA language for latency p95 per route and credits calculation method.

Next steps (short): 
- 2026-03-15 architecture review with SE to finalize warm pool sizing and scale policy (owner: Liam).
- AE to deliver a pricing delta for H100-only vs mixed-reserved plan + 12/24 month commits (owner: Samira).
- Security to validate data residency proof for upcoming EU launch (owner: Lantern Grove security).
